title: HLS playlist and segment handlers with signed links
name: Signed HLS delivery

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how the signed link checks are implemented across the two handlers? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
For a playlist line such as "seg0.ts" in the stored index.m3u8, what does ManifestHandler write to the response?
choices: The line unchanged, since the player resolves it relative to the playlist URL.
A rewritten URL under /segments/<id>/ with exp and sig query parameters; lines starting with # and blank lines are copied as they are.
Every line, including #EXTINF tag lines, replaced by a signed URL.
A redirect to the segment URL, with the playlist body omitted.

questions.prompt: A viewer holds a valid, unexpired signed link for the manifest of stream abc. Can they use the same exp and sig values on the manifest URL of stream xyz?
choices: Yes, because the signature covers only the expiry time and the shared key.
Yes, because ManifestHandler only validates the signature and the expiry, not the stream id.
No, because Sign hashes the viewer's session cookie together with the path.
No, because the signed message includes the request path, so the signature will not match for a different stream id.

questions.prompt: Suppose Signer.Sign is changed so the signed message also includes a version string, for example path + "|" + exp + "|v2". What must change for all newly issued links to keep working?
choices: Signer.Sign and the verification code in both ManifestHandler and SegmentHandler, because each handler builds the HMAC message itself.
Only Signer.Sign, since the handlers call into Signer to verify.
Only the two handlers, because Sign output is not used by them.
Nothing; the HMAC key is shared, so any message format verifies.
